subject: Private hosting feasibility — minimal-oncall path & gating questions
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private hosting feasibility — minimal-oncall path & gating questions

Team —

Thanks for the quick sync this morning. I wanted to capture the top-level asks and open questions so we can get a short decision readout for Sales/Legal by EOD next Tue (11/24). High-level: Acme wants a VPC-hosted/private install with an on-prem option down the road. They see the value in our Dedicated model but are asking for a private control plane with direct peering and a SOC2 summary.

Key asks for this thread:
- Minimal runbook we can ship for low-touch onboarding (what oncall coverage is required for M1?)
- Security gating: what evidence can we provide now vs. later (SOC2, audit logs, network diagram)
- Resourcing: what ENG/OPS FTEs do we need for the pilot (2-week onboarding + 6-week stabilization)

Attachments: initial network diagram (draft) and ops runbook stub attached for context.

Please reply with short bullets — what we can commit to for the pilot vs. needs a legal/PM exception.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network_diagram.vsdx (stub), ops_runbook_draft.pdf (stub)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — minimal-oncall path & gating questions

Kimberly —

Quick notes from infra/arch perspective (pilot constraints):
- Minimal path: we can support a private control plane + VPC peering where customer provides a routable subnet + NAT. No on-prem appliance required for pilot.
- Oncall: 0.25 FTE during onboarding (first 2 weeks) for infra tuning; 0.05–0.1 FTE steady-state for CI/infra alerts if we keep aggressive caching and KV limits. That assumes we use our quantized model builds (Q4) to reduce OOM risk.
- Security evidence: we can share a high-level SOC2 summary and network diagram today. Full SOC2 report or auditor artifacts require Legal approval to share and may need an NDA addendum.
- Known blockers: customer requires private EFS mount for model artifacts — that increases ops complexity (we'll need a secure S3/VPC endpoint pattern or an NFS pattern).

Action ask: Marcus, can you confirm ops staffing that matches 0.25 FTE onboarding / 0.1 steady-state? Lauren, can you confirm if Sales will accept a SOC2 summary + signed PD vs. full report?

Dev
Principal Architect — Inference Runtime

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — minimal-oncall path & gating questions

Team —

From a resourcing/engagement perspective (sales-side ask):
- Commercial will accept SOC2 summary + an engineer-signed evidence packet for pilot customers, provided Legal signs an evidence sharing addendum. That gets us across the line for procurement in most mid-market deals.
- Resource commitment for pilot: Sales can budget for 1x dedicated SE (0.5 FTE) + 0.25 FTE infra (Dev's ask) for the 8-week pilot. For renewals/expansion we should price a baseline "private maintenance" SKU (0.1 FTE included).
- Pricing note: because customer wants private control plane and peering, recommend we treat pilot as a billable POC with a capped support fee. I'll draft language for the SOW.

Lauren
Director, Commercial

Attachment: placeholder SOW language will be linked in HS record.

From: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — minimal-oncall path & gating questions

Kimberly —

Thanks for the update. Two quick asks from procurement to avoid delay: 1) Can you provide a SOC2 summary or a redacted report we can share with our internal security team? 2) We need a high-level network diagram showing egress/ingress points and where logs are retained for 90 days.

Also please confirm expected SOW cadence for the pilot and if there will be an on-site kickoff (we prefer a remote kickoff).

Jane Doe
Sourcing Manager, Acme Corp
procurement@acme.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — minimal-oncall path & gating questions

Jane + team —

We can provide the following this week:
- SOC2 summary (redacted) and a one-page evidence checklist (attached: soc2-summary.pdf).
- Network diagram (attached draft; see network_diagram.vsdx) showing peering and log egress to the customer's logging bucket — retention/ownership remains with Acme.
- Ops runbook (draft) with escalation points and the suggested 0.25 FTE onboarding coverage.

SOW cadence: Commercial will issue a capped POC SOW covering a 2-week onboarding + 6-week stabilization window. No on-site kickoff required for pilot per Acme preference; remote kickoff is fine.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Dev to finalize the runbook and confirm if the EFS/NFS ask can be replaced with a secure S3-backed pattern by EOD Wed (11/25).
2) Lauren to share draft SOW (HS-12345) and get Legal looped for the evidence addendum.
3) Marcus to confirm Ops FTE availability and start dates for onboarding.

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and the current network draft to this thread.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Attachments: soc2-summary.pdf (stub), network_diagram.vsdx (updated stub), ops_runbook_draft.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private hosting feasibility — minimal-oncall path & gating questions

Kimberly / team —

Confirmed: Ops can cover the 0.25 FTE onboarding window starting 12/01 and provide 0.1 FTE steady-state support post-pilot. We will add a short runbook task to the oncall queue so the engineer covering the pilot has immediate escalation contacts.

Dev — I agree we should avoid EFS unless strictly required. If you can validate the secure S3-backed pattern by EOD Wed, I'll sign off on the staffing and we can proceed with Commercial's draft SOW.

Marcus
Senior Manager, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
